# dsh-fluid-chat-width
Fluid conversation width for the DeepSeek Harness web GUI.

The chat column stops being pinned to a fixed reading measure and follows the
window instead: **colu

mn width − 64px, capped at 1560px, floored at 640px**. No
settings page, no button — resize the wind
ow and the column tracks it.
## What it does

The DSH web client sizes its conversation column from a fixed measure and lets
the built-in drag han

dles override it with an inline
`--dsh-chat-user-width` on the conversation root. This plugin publis

hes that
same custom property from a `ResizeObserver` on the column, so:

- **Fluid by default** — the column is `min(columnWidth − 64, 1560)` on every
resize, never narrower

than the app's own 640px floor.
- **Drag handles still win** — a handle writes a deeper inline decl

aration, which
legitimately overrides the published value. Dragging is unaffected; the value
you dra

g to is what you get.
- **Stale preferences are cleared once per boot** — the client persists a fixe

d
width in `localStorage["dsh.conversation.contentWidth"]`. On startup this
plugin removes that key

and strips any inline echo already published, so a
leftover pinned width from an earlier drag cannot
silently defeat it.

Embedded conversations are left alone: they define their own content width and
ignore `--dsh-chat-us

er-width`. Only the main chat region is targeted
(`[data-conversation-region="chat"] > [data-convers

the main chat region is targeted
(`[data-conversation-region="chat"] > [data-conversation-scroll]`).

## Uninstall
[代码示例省略，未执行]

If you had dragged a handle before installing, the preference key was cleared on
boot. Nothing else

is left behind — the plugin writes no files, registers no
routes, and touches no storage except remo

he plugin writes no files, registers no
routes, and touches no storage except removing that one key.
## How it is built
Two faces, no build step, no runtime dependencies:
| File | Face | Role |
| `index.js` | host (Node) | Deliberately empty. Satisfies the plugin shape so the bundle patch can

mount the package into the web roster. |
| `client.js` | browser | The whole plugin: one `ResizeObse

rver`, one custom property. A hand-written `window.__ModuleLoader__.load` closure factory. |
| `cord
is.patch.yml` | bundle patch | Inserts the `dsh.client` row into the profile's layer stack. |

There is no bundler and no transpiler — `client.js` ships as written, which is
why the source you re
ad here is the source that runs.
